title: "Software engineering is not about writing code" — Benoit Schillings, Google DeepMind VP of Research
talk_summary: A DeepMind VP argues that code generation is now essentially solved and the real engineering bottleneck has shifted to specification, architecture, verification, and managing complexity at scale. He sketches implications: guardrails/security, better evals than pass/fail benchmarks, planning/decomposition, and self-play-style verifiable challenge loops.

takeaways.technique: Shift review from style/syntax to design adequacy and security
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues that since writing code is cheap, the scarce human/model effort should go to whether the code is what was actually wanted and whether it is safe, not to line-level syntax.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to think at least as much about code security and the implication of a piece of code than on the code writing itself

takeaways.technique: Open-ended scored evals instead of pass/fail
takeaways.what_they_do: Criticizes benchmarks that only check 'runs and produces right output' and proposes open-ended problems with a continuous loss (e.g. best lossless compressor scored by compressed size + source size).
takeaways.evidence_quote: threebench verifies if a piece of code runs and produce the right output. That's only a small part

takeaways.what_they_do: Identifies correct planning and problem decomposition as the skill models still lack and that must be taught/forced for complex systems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: teach models how to do correct planning in front of a problem. How do you look at a very complex problem and decide what is the right decomposition

takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that model-driven vuln discovery will be endless and the real goal is teaching models to write correct-by-construction code, acknowledging it is very context dependent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of detecting the vulnerability and then suggesting some fix how about teaching model to write correct things from the start

takeaways.what_they_do: Describes models generating their own challenges, judging validity, and iterating — the AlphaZero-style loop — as the path to better coding ability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they can create their own challenge. They can judge the validity of the answer

takeaways.what_they_do: Suggests chain-of-tokens is insufficient and that block diagrams / data-flow representations may be needed for complex reasoning about code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: code writing is a very visual activity ... the block diagram of what you're doing or the flow of data
